posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
The help file (F1 -> Asset Standards) is fairly comprehensive on this matter. It's not perfect and does omit a few little details though.
Characters
– can be any size (a multiple of 12 wide, 8 high for a large sheet, or a multiple of 3 wide, 4 high for a single-character sheet with $), but the standard size is 576x384 for a tile-sized sheet containing 8 characters.
Faces
– can be any size (576 wide and a multiple of 144 high). Each face is 144x144 and there are four faces per row; standard size is 2 rows (576x288) but, contrary to what the document claims, you can add as many rows as you want.
Sideview Battlers
– Can be any size (a multiple of 9 wide, 6 high), but the standard size (for RTP-sized chibi battlers) is 576x384, as noted in F1 -> Side-view Character Standards.
Tilesets
– There are 6 different sizes for tilesets – the Asset Standards covers them all in detail. As far as I can tell, nothing will break if you make a tilesheet smaller than the specified size – the game will just internally resize it to the required size and go from there.
System Images
– All of these are a fixed size, except for IconSet, which allows you to add as many rows as you want (as far as I know). Balloons are "tile sized", so each frame is 48x48. Side-view weapons are meant to match up to side-view characters… the Asset Standards are vague on this, but I think they can be any size? The standard size seems to be 576x384 with a cell size of 96x64.
Others
– Again, the Asset Standards covers everything else in quite some detail.
EDIT: Added a note that tilesheet sizes are maximum, not exact.
